learningObjective: Explain what chunked prefill is and why it improves multi-tenant serving under mixed prefill+decode load.
stem: Chunked prefill in modern LLM serving systems addresses which problem, and how?

options.text: Long prefill requests block decode requests behind them, spiking TPOT for concurrent short-completion requests. Chunked prefill splits a prefill of length P into chunks (e.g., 512 tokens each) and lets each chunk share a model-forward iteration with ongoing decode requests, keeping per-token latency bounded while making forward progress on the long prefill.

Prefill sometimes exceeds available HBM for the intermediate activations of the whole prompt at once; chunked prefill processes the prompt in windows so that only one chunk of activations lives in memory at a time. This is the sole reason for chunked prefill.

Chunked prefill splits the prompt across multiple GPUs via tensor parallelism; each GPU handles one chunk of the prompt independently, and the chunks are recombined at the attention step. It is essentially a form of context parallelism.
Chunked prefill converts the prefill matmul into smaller matmuls that fit tensor-core tile sizes better; the primary benefit is arithmetic throughput improvement of the prefill phase itself.

explanation: Chunked prefill (an SGLang / vLLM / TRT-LLM inflight-batching feature) is a scheduling policy: a long prefill is broken into chunks (typical 512-2048 tokens per chunk) and each chunk is packed into the same model-forward iteration as concurrent decode requests. This keeps TPOT bounded for other tenants while the long prefill makes forward progress. It is orthogonal to how the prefill kernel is written; it is a scheduling / batching decision.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: chunked prefill's role in preventing TPOT spikes under mixed workload.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: activation memory can motivate chunking, but it is not the primary motivation in modern serving stacks.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: describes context parallelism / sequence parallelism, not chunked prefill.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: prefill is already compute-bound and tile-friendly; chunking is about scheduling, not tiling.

assumptions: Serving system supports continuous / inflight batching so a chunk can be co-scheduled with decode requests.
Chunk size is a tunable parameter, typically 512-2048 tokens.
nonImplications: Does not imply that chunked prefill speeds up prefill in isolation; it may slow it slightly due to overhead.
Does not imply prefill activation memory is never a concern; it is, especially for very long prompts.

distractorRationales.B: Names a secondary motivation as primary.

performanceClaim.scope: Chunked prefill scheduling and its TPOT benefit under mixed workloads
